threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the Lido' refers to the one in Clapton, not realizing there’s a whole other kind of lido in Hackney.
Saw an old man on the 196 last night feeding a pigeon his chips, while everyone else was glued to their phones. Strange how life carries on around us.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a wild pigeon casually pecking at a kebab near the bakery at Sonnenallee, just another day in Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you pop into a bar that's also a gallery, then end the night at a techno club in a former dog biscuit factory. Classic Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their instinct to avoid BART on Fridays—everyone in the know knows the Transbay Tube's a mess after 5 PM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full business suit napping on a Muni seat next to a woman in a tie-dye dress, both oblivious to the rush hour chaos around them. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for selfies, but locals actually linger over village gossip and weekend vermut in the shade.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle to use the dialect—asking for 'una cervesa' instead of 'un birra' at the bar.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston is just a trendy spot for brunch rather than a battleground for vintage record shops and late-night kebabs.
Caught a guy on the 415 last night lecturing the driver on the best way to avoid traffic. Strangest mix of confidence and cluelessness I've seen.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in flip-flops arguing with a street musician about the best spot for a coffee popup.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg has spontaneous block parties? Just a group of neighbors, some grills, and music. No one planning it, just spring in the air.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can name the exact date the taco truck on Cortland gets its carne asada special. Tourists just call it ‘the taco place.’

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo juggling at the Civic Center stop while waiting for the 21. Only in this city do you get that kind of unexpected show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and fancy cafes, but locals know it’s about the hidden corners with street art and spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by the way they insist on ordering 'café con leche' instead of just 'un café'.
